latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan · no trades · everything we own is healthy, nothing new is cheap enough to buy yet
latest_messages.body: Research-only morning (market closed). Backdrop is a quiet, slightly cautious drift: futures ~flat, calm VIX ~15, but the 10-year yield still ~5.3% (a multi-decade high) keeps ResMed/Republic pressured — nothing wrong at either company, just the rate backdrop. Oil +1% is a tailwind for BP (also got a fresh price-target raise to $56); BP, Nvidia and the S&P floor are green. Microsoft ~$530 is still above our $515-522 buy band and past the $525 don't-chase line, so per your plan I wait. No other name is both high-quality AND on a calm entry today, so I'm keeping our one open slot open. One event today: Fed meeting notes at 1:00 CT. Equity ~$96,256; cash ~11%; 0 of 3 weekly buys used; ResMed is the thinnest cushion (~3.9%).

latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $96,444 · day +0.41% · SPY +0.53% · alpha −0.12% — green day, market edged us by a hair
latest_messages.body: No trades. We made +$391 (+0.41%); SPY +0.53%, so we trailed by ~0.1pt. BP, Nvidia and the index sleeve were green; our two rate-sensitive defensives (ResMed, Republic) drifted lower on the high long-term rate — business is fine, it's the rate backdrop. Week-to-date we're even with the market (+1.21% vs +1.23%). ResMed is the thinnest cushion (~3.7%); watching Fed minutes Wed.

latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady and green — no changes, and Microsoft is still too hot to buy
latest_messages.body: Noon risk check, no trades. We're up ~$532 today (+0.55%) and the S&P 500 is +0.64%, so we're about even with the market. BP (+1.1%) and Nvidia (+1.4%) both flipped green, leaving just ResMed (-2.8%) and Republic Services (-1.2%) in the red — both still comfortably above their safety-sells (~4.3% and ~5.9% of room). Microsoft is ~$532, above our $515-522 buy band and past the $525 don't-chase line, so per your plan I did nothing. 4 stops resting GTC, SPY unencumbered. Next: the 3:00 CT close with your scorecard. Cash ~$10,546 (~11%); 0 of 3 weekly buys used; slot still reserved for Microsoft.

latest_messages.headline: Open · no trades · Microsoft ran away from our buy price; all holdings healthy
latest_messages.body: Confirmed the market open, then re-ran our one armed plan (Microsoft) against live prices. MSFT opened ~$530.87 — above the $515-522 buy band and past our $525 don't-chase line — so no buy, by the plan's own rules. No sell signals, no stop breaches, no +5% conversions. 4 stops resting GTC, SPY unencumbered. Equity $96,328 (+0.29% intraday), cash ~11%. Waiting for a genuine MSFT dip or a fresh clean setup.

MSFT still above its $515-522 buy band ($525 close) — armed but no chase. All 4 holdings healthy, stops in place. Equity ~$96,189, cash ~11%.

latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $96,048 · day +0.80% · SPY +0.67% · alpha +0.13% — a green day, and we edged the market 🐂
latest_messages.body: Final numbers at the bell: we finished UP ~$760 (+0.80%) and the S&P 500 was +0.67%, so we came out a touch ahead of the market today. No trades. The win came mostly from our S&P 500 'market floor' fund (+1.11%): because I didn't sell any of it to buy Microsoft, we kept full market exposure on an up day — the main reason we beat the index. BP (+0.27%) and Nvidia (+0.85%) also finished green. ResMed (-2.52%) and Republic Services (-2.37%) stayed our two soft spots (rate-sensitive), but both sit safely above their automatic safety-sells. On Microsoft: your approved plan said buy ONLY on a calm dip into $515-522 and do NOT chase at $525+. Microsoft closed at $525.18 — above that line — so, exactly per your plan, I did not buy and did not trim the S&P floor. The plan stays ready for a real dip.

latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady and green — no changes, and I passed on Microsoft again (still too hot to chase)
latest_messages.body: Noon risk check — no trades. We're UP ~$739 today (+0.78%) and beating the S&P 500 so far (it's +0.57%). Our two weakest holds this morning, ResMed and Republic Services, both bounced back, so they're further from their safety-sells now (cushions ~4.6% and ~4.9%). I looked at Microsoft one more time: it cooled a bit but is still ~$525, ~8% above its 50-day trend line, still stretched. My rule is to buy quality on a CALM entry, not chase a pop. Its earnings are ~Oct 28, so there's no rush.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trade yet — held off on Microsoft because it jumped too far, too fast
latest_messages.body: Market opened; everything's healthy and we're about flat (+$34). I planned to buy Microsoft but decided NOT to at the open — on purpose. Microsoft got even better news overnight (a fresh upgrade to Buy, $665 target, plus Wells Fargo naming it a top idea), which made the stock gap up +2.7% while the market barely moved. My rule is to buy quality on a calm entry, not chase a one-morning pop to a fresh high. I'll re-check at midday — if Microsoft settles, I'll buy a ~10-12% starter with a −7% safety net, funded by trimming one S&P 500 slice. If it keeps running, I wait.
